# DockPreviewGeometry's failed-projection arm never fails a projection

## Context

Found while adding the `applyOperationJson_` trigger to the `dock-preview-geometry` fixture for #19516 (defect-note 2026-10-09 18:16Z). `DockPreviewGeometry.spec.mjs` › `the settle guard survives a FAILED projection` › `a projection that throws leaves the guard satisfiable` arms `failNextProjection: true` through `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs`. No fixture defines `failNextProjection`: `git log -S failNextProjection` finds only the spec's own commit, `2842dd6b2b` (#18203). `setConfigs` writes a plain property that nothing reads.

- **Before #19516:** the `applyOperationJson` trigger the arm sets next did not exist either. No projection ran at all, and `busy === false` held trivially.
- **Since #19516**, which added that trigger: the arm runs a successful projection. The failure path it names is still never taken.

## The Problem

The arm guards a real class. The settle guard's `dockProjectionBusy` latched when it was paired across two hooks, because `refreshDockWorkspace` skips its second hook on the typed projection-failure path, on the destroyed guard, and on a throw. The fixture's `try/finally` closes that class (#18179/#18203, the RA I raised then). An arm that never fails a projection cannot catch a regression of that `finally`.

Prior art explains the gap (Grace's 09-03 session, Memory Core):
- The arm was mutation-checked locally, with an armed throw and a failure counter. Grace's own note: "A control asserting an ABSENCE needs a second signal proving the CAUSE fired."
- Afterwards, a `git checkout -- app.mjs` restore ate uncommitted work. The lost `finally` was caught by grep; the lost failure seam was not.
- The committed spec kept calling the seam and asserting only the absence.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/component/apps/dock-preview-geometry/app.mjs`: `PreviewGeometryWorkspace` brackets `refreshDockWorkspace` in `try/finally` (`dockProjectionBusy`) and counts completions in `afterRefreshDockWorkspace` (`dockProjectionSettles`). Since #19516 it also has `applyOperationJson_`.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` calls `beforeRefreshDockWorkspace` before every projection, retries included. On the typed failure path it fires `dockProjectionFailed` (`{error, isRetry, recovery}`), returns `null` without `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`, and schedules **one** clean re-projection. A retry that fails too is not retried again.
- `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` types a rejected host flight in phases 2–4 as `isDockProjectionFailure`.

## The Fix

> **Revised 2026-10-09, before the PR:** one failure is not enough. Its retry completes and clears even a paired-hook latch, so the arm could not tell the two shapes apart. Failing the retry too leaves no completion, and only the `finally` can clear the guard.

1. **Fixture:** a reactive `failProjections_` (a count). Each of the next projections arms, in `beforeRefreshDockWorkspace`, a one-shot rejection of the dock host's second update flight, which is the typed failure path. A `dockProjectionFailures` counter, fed by the workspace's own `dockProjectionFailed` event, is the second signal.
2. **Spec:** set `failProjections: 2` and commit. Then poll until the state is `{busy: false, failures: 2, settles: <unchanged>}`, replacing the fixed 1200 ms sleep.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: the arm proves the cause fired (`dockProjectionFailures === 2`: the projection and its one retry) before it asserts the absence of a latch.
- [ ] AC-2: it is red when the fixture's `try/finally` is replaced by the paired-hook shape (busy set in `beforeRefreshDockWorkspace`, cleared in `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`), and green with the `finally`. Record the mutation run.
- [ ] AC-3: no fixed sleep remains in the arm; `DockPreviewGeometry.spec.mjs` and `DockShellRetirement.spec.mjs`, which share the fixture, pass.

## Out of Scope

- The settle guard's design (#18179 settled it).
- The other `DockPreviewGeometry` arms.
